requiredChecksCutover.decidedBy: INFRA-490 architect, dispatch://INFRA-520/comment/504b64a2-cbd6-4eec-97e4-4b5ed412a9b1 (item 6); merge queue: INFRA-520 spec v7 at the INFRA Legion controller's direction
order: 1. #2316 merges under today's ruleset: its head reports lint, typecheck and test (ci.yaml's job ids, fail-open when changes fails), ci-ok and pr-title.

2. Interim: the ruleset still requires lint, typecheck, test, pr-title. Every pull request pushed after the merge reports ci-ok too: a pull_request run takes ci.yaml from the merge ref, so an open pull request reports ci-ok at its next push or reopen without a merge of main. The other router jobs are advisory until the flip.
3. Flip when every open, non-draft, non-conflicting pull request updated in the last 24 hours reports ci-ok at its head, or 24 hours after the merge, whichever comes first.
4. Session 01a16962 makes the edit with GITHUB_PERSONAL_ADMIN_PAT (one edit: required checks and the merge queue).
5. After the flip, check no open non-draft non-conflicting pull request is BLOCKED for a missing check, and watch the first pull requests through the queue.
requiredChecksCutover.flipConditionCommand: since=$(date -u -d '24 hours ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ); gh pr list -R sjawhar/legion --state open --limit 300 --json number,isDraft,mergeable,headRefOid,updatedAt --jq --arg since "$since" '.[] | select((.isDraft|not) and .mergeable != "CONFLICTING" and .updatedAt >= $since) | "\(.number) \(.headRefOid)"' | while read -r n sha; do c=$(gh api "repos/sjawhar/legion/commits/$sha/check-runs?check_name=ci-ok" --jq .total_count); [ "$c" -gt 0 ] || echo "missing ci-ok: #$n $sha"; done   # flip when it prints nothing, or 24 hours after the merge
requiredChecksCutover.adminCheck: With the admin token: GET https://api.github.com/repos/sjawhar/legion must answer permissions.admin == true (e.g. curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_PERSONAL_ADMIN_PAT" https://api.github.com/repos/sjawhar/legion | jq .permissions.admin). Note: a pane's `gh` wrapper refuses a set GH_TOKEN, so use curl (or the real gh binary) inside `agent-secrets GITHUB_PERSONAL_ADMIN_PAT -- sh -c '…'`.

mergeQueue.settings: check_response_timeout_minutes 150 (above the slowest selected job: dispatch-memory's 75-minute timeout, the Playwright dispatch job's 50-minute p90, plus up to an hour of runner queue); grouping_strategy ALLGREEN (every pull request must satisfy the required checks); max_entries_to_build 5 and max_entries_to_merge 5 (batching allowed, about 34 merges a day); min_entries_to_merge 1 with min_entries_to_merge_wait_minutes 5; merge_method SQUASH (the pull_request rule allows only squash).
mergeQueue.requiredChecksOnTheGroup: ci-ok: ci.yaml runs on merge_group; changes diffs merge_group.base_sha..head_sha (dorny/paths-filter v4.0.3 src/main.ts 126-138) and ci-ok reports on the group commit. pr-title: GitHub's docs say a required check that is not reported on the merge group fails it ('The merge will fail as the required status check will not be reported', https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue#triggering-merge-group-checks-with-github-actions), so pr-title.yaml runs on merge_group and re-checks the text of the pull request the queue branch names.

trickyParts: A skipped job reports success: ci-ok passes only when changes succeeded, and lint, typecheck and test run when changes fails (fail-open) because the ruleset requires them until the flip.
Scratch pull requests must be stacked on legion/INFRA-520: a scratch against main would carry ci.yaml in its diff and select every job.
worker_image's exclusions need the step's predicate-quantifier some-with-excludes: under some a `!` pattern matches every file outside it; no other filter may carry a `!`.
Running go list inside packages/envoy/infra rewrites packages/envoy/infra/go.work.sum; restore it after the coverage script.
GitHub's queue was 160-210 runs deep on 2026-10-27; scratch runs waited up to three hours for a runner.

A line whose step directory differs from its Run's falls to the modules of both, since a cd in the script may move it to either; above every module (the repository root) that is each module of the go.work there.
Exact entries pin the step's whole run: script and its working directory; the Pack entry's architectures come from go-release-targets.json, the file its loop reads.
